dcs_bresar_mijatovic_2026.paper: Bresar & Mijatovic (2026), 'Diffeomorphic Markov Chain Monte Carlo: fast mixing for heavy-tailed distributions', arXiv:2608.04284v1 (submitted 4 Aug 2026)
dcs_bresar_mijatovic_2026.status: not run: no official code found
searched: arXiv abstract, HTML full text and PDF of 2608.04284v1: no code, repository or supplementary link
arXiv 'Code, Data, Media' tab: only generic links, no ancillary files; Hugging Face papers page: 404
GitHub: no repositories for 'diffeomorphic mcmc', 'diffeomorphic contraction sampler', 'contraction sampler'; github.com/aleks-mijatovic holds only a website repository
Authors' pages (Warwick staff page, aleks-mijatovic.github.io) and the CUHK and PolyU talk pages: arXiv and YouTube links only
Related preprint arXiv:2512.18255 (Bresar, Mijatovic, Roberts): no code
dcs_bresar_mijatovic_2026.why_no_reimplementation: The paper specifies the radial contraction, the Mobius recentring and the ball-walk and hit-and-run kernels, but not the variational-tuning settings (steps, batch size, learning rate, initial values), the ball-walk radius, the slice-sampler settings, or the beta, mu and R used for its posteriordb runs. Its published comparisons are at matched wall time, so a home-made version could not be checked against them and would not be 'their method'.

metric_definitions.total_grad_evals: target gradient evaluations, warm-up and adaptation or flow training included (see telemetry.grad_eval_accounting)
metric_definitions.tail_ess: coordinate mean of ArviZ rank-normalised tail-ESS
metric_definitions.split_rhat: max over coordinates of rank-normalised split R-hat
metric_definitions.combined_rhat: max of split and folded R-hat over coordinates
metric_definitions.tail_prob_abs_err_p01: mean over coordinates of |P_hat(x_j <= q_j(0.01)) - 0.01|, q_j the exact marginal quantile
metric_definitions.tail_prob_mcse_*: mean over coordinates of the MCSE of that tail-indicator mean (ArviZ, ESS-based); if a tail is never visited, the i.i.d. binomial standard error at the true probability
metric_definitions.tail_prob_rms_z_*: root mean square over coordinates of error / MCSE (about 1 when MCSEs are honest)
metric_definitions.q99_rel_error: mean over coordinates of |q_hat(0.99) - q(0.99)| / |q(0.99)| (noisy on Cauchy-like coordinates)
metric_definitions.wall_clock_time: seconds for the whole run, JIT compilation included

notes: Every arm gets the same per-seed initial positions, Uniform(-2, 2)^d per chain (initial_positions); nutpie assigns the rows to chains in the order it asks for them.

Every arm uses maximum tree depth 10 and target acceptance 0.8. nutpie_flow keeps nutpie's flow default divergence threshold (max_energy_error 20, versus 1000 in the other arms), so its divergence counts are not directly comparable.

nutpie runs through nutpie.compiled_pyfunc.from_pyfunc: each gradient is a Python call into a jitted JAX function, nutpie's own JAX-backend route. That per-gradient overhead is absent from nutpie's compiled numba and Stan backends, so nutpie's tail-ESS per second here understates what those backends reach.
Wall-clock times include JIT compilation and, for the flow arms, flow compilation and training. Chains run one after another in every arm except arcsinh_nuts, which vmaps its chains.
Paired ratios divide an arm's per-seed metric by stock_nuts' on the same target and seed; their median and IQR are over seeds.
